summary: The escape mechanism and its tests are sound; the cap still refuses unargued, an argued cap still blocks a major, and no object-store request rate is touched. Two prose defects block: (1) the 8-to-7 flip the commit says it reverted is STILL PERFORMED, in backlog M4.21, which this diff changes from 8 to 7 -- so review.md's record of the split is wrong the moment it lands and three separate disclosures describing the flip as a discarded draft are false about the staged bytes; (2) M4.26 attributes an index read to `git show :` that appears nowhere in the gate, contradicting M4.31 in the same diff.

findings.title: THE 8-TO-7 FLIP IS STILL IN THE DIFF. It was moved out of check-reviewed.sh and left in the backlog row this commit rewrites, and three places in the same diff assert it was only ever a draft.
findings.finding: `git show HEAD:docs/internal/product/backlog.md | grep -o 'violated on . of 12'` gives `violated on 8 of 12`; `git show :docs/internal/product/backlog.md | grep -o 'violated on . of 12'` gives `violated on 7 of 12`. The single occurrence is inside the M4.21 row itself: '...weakens a cap that exists because rule 12 was violated on 8 of 12 tasks when nothing counted' becomes '...on 7 of 12 tasks...'. So the staged bytes DO move the measured number in the direction that weakens the case for the cap the same commit loosens -- in the row that owns the loosening. Consequences, all in the staged bytes: (a) check-reviewed.sh:37-43 says 'The higher figure is kept', and it is not kept, only relocated; (b) review.md:87 records the split as '`check-reviewed.sh` and backlog M0.47 say 8 ... `review_rounds.py` says 7', which becomes false on landing because backlog M4.21 will also say 7 and the count of dissenters is 2-vs-2, not 2-vs-1; (c) review.md:88-92 and check-reviewed.sh:38 both describe the flip in the past tense -- 'a draft of the commit that wrote this paragraph quietly changed the 8 to a 7' -- so the disclosure that is supposed to make the flip visible is itself inaccurate about the diff it sits in, which is one worse than the unannounced flip. The fix is one character in one row plus extending review.md:87's enumeration if the 7 is kept deliberately.
findings.failure_scenario: The next author to weigh whether the round cap is worth its escape greps `of 12` and finds 7 in review_rounds.py and 7 in the M4.21 row -- the two documents nearest the mechanism -- against 8 in a shell comment and in M0.47. The majority reading is the lower figure, review.md's paragraph explaining the split lists the wrong holders, and the paragraph's own claim that the flip was a discarded draft stops anyone re-measuring. Neither number is reconstructible from the tree (AGENTS.md non-negotiable 2's 'never move a threshold in the direction that weakens its gate' applied to the evidence for the threshold), so the drift is permanent.

findings.title: M4.26 ATTRIBUTES THE INDEX READ TO A PRIMITIVE THAT IS NOT IN THE GATE, and M4.31 in the same diff says so.
findings.finding: M4.26 states: 'M4.21 closed exactly this hole for its new `rounds:` key -- reading the INDEX via `git show :` -- and left it open fourteen lines below.' `git show :scripts/check-reviewed.sh | grep -n 'git show'` returns nothing: the gate decides at line 136 with `git diff --cached -- baselines/review.txt | awk ...`. M4.31, added by this same commit, says exactly that and prescribes `git show :baselines/review.txt` against `git show HEAD:baselines/review.txt` as the FIX that M4.21 did NOT ship ('M4.21 shipped the TEXT half of this ... and left the primitive'). So two rows added in one commit contradict each other about what the code does, and the one that is wrong is the one a future author will read as a worked example. The substantive half of M4.26's sentence is true and pinned (`aROUNDSLineOnlyInTheWORKTREEOfASTAGEDFileDoesNOTLiftTheCap`); only the named primitive is false. Also note M4.21's own row says the key is 'matched against the INDEX rather than the worktree', which understates it -- `git diff --cached` matches against the index AND against HEAD, which is precisely M4.31's 'a THIRD question'.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M4.26 (three fixes: read the index, document the keys, require a reason) opens check-reviewed.sh looking for the `git show :` pattern the row says is fourteen lines above the hole, does not find it, and either (a) copies the `git diff --cached` shape into the finding-argue path -- reproducing M4.31's measured defect in the heavier of the two argue paths, where it silences blocking findings rather than a round count -- or (b) burns the round establishing which of two rows added by the same commit is describing the tree. This is the doc-asserting-absent-behaviour class M0.51 and M0.66 exist for, recurring in the commit that closes them.

findings.title: M4.31's 'thirteen red records' is 15, and this commit is what made it stale.
findings.finding: M4.31 argues its own deferral with 'adding a test to `ReviewRoundCapTest` re-keys all thirteen red records -- `tdd_scan.py`'s remainder half spans the whole file.' The staged file has 15 `@Test` methods and `.harness/tdd/red.json` carries 15 `ReviewRoundCapTest#...` ids, because this round added `anArgumentInADIFFERENTSTAGEDFileDoesNOTLiftTheCap` and `verdictsThatNameNOTASKRefuseRatherThanCountingAsROUNDZERO`. The count is the row's cost argument, so it is load-bearing. Same recurrence the M4.21 row itself flags two rows above ('THIS SENTENCE SAID FIVE, THEN NINE') and that M4.12's row argues against counts for.
findings.failure_scenario: The M4.31 implementer sizes the work from 'thirteen', finds 15 (more by then), and either doubts the row or re-derives the cost -- the row's only quantitative argument for having been split out is wrong by two on the day it lands.

findings.title: The M4.21 row's 'what is covered' enumeration omits exactly the two cases this round added.
findings.finding: The row lists: cap firing and not firing, exact key match, key with no reason, argument for another task, unstaged argument, worktree-only line in a staged file, line only in HISTORY, line only as diff CONTEXT, decoy FILENAME, verdicts disagreeing about the task, and an argued cap still blocking a major -- thirteen behaviours for the thirteen tests that existed at round 6. Neither WHICH FILE the argument must live in (`anArgumentInADIFFERENTSTAGEDFileDoesNOTLiftTheCap`, the pathspec) nor the no-task refusal (`verdictsThatNameNOTASKRefuseRatherThanCountingAsROUNDZERO`) appears, though the row's closing state is `done` and both were added to close round-6 majors. The row deliberately enumerates behaviours rather than a count precisely so this could not happen.
findings.failure_scenario: A later reader auditing whether the pathspec or the no-task guard is constrained reads the closed row's coverage list, finds neither named, and re-derives (or re-files) a major that round 6 already found and round 7 already closed -- the round-6 near miss in M4.34, arriving from the row instead of from a truncated packet.

findings.title: Rule 12 states 'ADDED by this commit' as an exact requirement, and the caveat that it is not exact is only in the place the same paragraph says agents do not read.
findings.finding: Rule 12's new text gives the three requirements and adds: 'Stated here because the milestone loop reads this file and the skills, not the gate's output, so an agent that stops at the cap never sees the remedy printed at the moment of need.' But 'ADDED by this commit' is the primitive M4.31 measures as wrong in both directions -- a MOVED committed line re-renders as an addition and re-arms the escape, and an argument that has landed can never carry a later round. `check-reviewed.sh` DOES print that caveat ('but see M4.31: a later edit that makes git re-render the committed line as added can re-arm it, which is measured and not yet fixed'). Rule 12 does not, so the file the paragraph nominates as authoritative-for-agents is the one that overstates the property. One clause referencing M4.31 closes it.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent at the cap follows rule 12, reasons that the argument it added last commit is now committed and therefore cannot argue again, and reaches for `SKIP=check-reviewed` -- the exact state M4.21 was filed to end -- or conversely trusts 'ADDED by this commit' and does not notice that reordering the baseline file silently re-armed a landed exception for an unrelated commit.

findings.title: Rule 12b's private-index prescription is unverified, incomplete for the review step, and is scope this task did not ask for.
findings.finding: The new 12b paragraph adds a fourth lost review and prescribes `GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp -d)/idx git read-tree HEAD` then staging only your own paths, concluding 'so neither session can sweep in the other's files or void the other's review'. Two gaps. (a) It cannot hold for the review itself unless the REVIEWER also runs under the same `GIT_INDEX_FILE`: `review.sh` and `check-reviewed.sh` both compute the hash from `git diff --cached`, which reads whatever index the environment names, and the paragraph does not say the reviewer must inherit it. Nor does it address pre-commit, which performs its own index manipulation around hooks. Neither is demonstrated anywhere in the tree, so this is a mechanism asserted rather than measured -- the class this milestone keeps filing rows about. (b) It is unrelated to M4.21's subject (a printed remedy the code did not implement), and M0.21 already owns 'review.sh refuses a verdict whose index moved while the review was in flight'. AGENTS.md: never widen scope silently. Note also that this commit is its own counter-example -- HEAD moved from 461dd53 to 4ca1865 under this very round.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent follows the prescription, commits through a private index, and the pre-commit run either fails confusingly (the hooks see a different index from the one that was staged) or passes over a hash no reviewer ever saw. Either way a standard was followed and the guarantee it promised did not hold, which is worse than the prose warning it replaced.

findings.title: The second `review_rounds.py` call swallows the exit status the same file spends six lines condemning, and the guard below it then reports the wrong cause.
findings.finding: `TASK=$(python3 scripts/review_rounds.py "$SHA" --task 2>/dev/null || true)` discards both stderr and the status. Twelve lines above, the comment block explains at length why `|| echo 0` was removed from the ROUNDS call: 'A gate that cannot tell "nothing recorded" from "the records contradict each other" is the shape this whole file exists against.' The same script then reintroduces `2>/dev/null || true` for the identical invocation. It is safe only because the ROUNDS call succeeded moments earlier -- an ordering dependency, not a guarantee, and this checkout demonstrably has concurrent sessions writing `.harness/review/`. If a second verdict for `$SHA` naming a different task is recorded between the two calls, the disagreement `SystemExit` is swallowed, `TASK` is empty, and line 93 refuses with 'verdicts exist for the staged bytes but name no task -- recorded without --task' -- naming the wrong cause for a stop the file went to some trouble to make nameable. Resolving the task once and reusing it, or applying the same `|| { RC=$?; ... }` shape, closes it.
findings.failure_scenario: Two agent sessions review in one checkout (M4.27 and this task's own round history record exactly that). One records under a mistyped task while the gate is running. The commit refuses -- correctly -- with a message that sends the author to `review.sh record --task`, when the artifacts actually contradict each other and a human needs to look at both verdicts.

notes: Cost lens: nothing here issues an object-store request. The diff is two harness scripts, one standard, one backlog file and a buildSrc test over a scratch git repository. No LIST is added, no idle path acquires a request, and no request rate scales with records, shards, partitions or indices. Object-store request rate is unaffected.

Answering the three questions the change implicitly asks, judged from the bytes: the cap still REFUSES an unargued third round; an argued cap still blocks an unresolved major (`warn` in lib.sh does not set FAILED, so control falls through to the per-role findings loop, and `anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKSAnUnresolvedMajor` pins it); the pathspec, the exact-field match, the reason requirement and the added-line requirement are each pinned by a test that dies on its own mutation.

Verified independently rather than taken from the prose: `git log --grep=SKIP=check-reviewed` returns exactly the nine commits review.md names (M4.0 0837f34, M4.1 44400b5, M4.3 74254f6, M4.3b d9a3c22, M4.4b 6871e7f, M4.6c 3a5ed79, M4.6e 461dd53, M4.19 2953b5a, M4.20 2e0f1d9), and only 2e0f1d9 ('THE THIRD TIME') and 2953b5a ('THE SECOND TIME') carry an ordinal, as rule 12 says. Grouping distinct diff_sha256 by task across .harness/review gives 22 tasks over the cap with M4.12 at 12 and M0.13 at 11, and 90 of 396 verdict files (22.7%) carry no task -- 'at least 22' and 'roughly a quarter' both hold, and omitting the denominator is the right call since it read 82 for me.

review_rounds.py's docstring is accurate as staged, including the parenthetical correcting REFUSED vs COMPARED: check-reviewed.sh compares `ROUNDS > 2` first and consults the argument inside that branch. M0.51's closing note matches the code. M0.66's amendment matches the code -- item (3) is what survives, `rounds_for` still counts every hash carrying the task -- and its self-correction about the mis-aimed accusation is right on the row's own wording.

Not filed, for the record: the `ls ".harness/review/$SHA."*.json` conjunct in the no-task guard can never be false where it sits, because the role-existence loop above it `finish`es on any missing verdict file. It is harmless belt-and-braces, not a defect.
